reason: The Book of Esther is uniquely characterized by the complete absence of any explicit mention of Yahweh (God) throughout the entire text. Furthermore, the narrative arc depicts the Jewish people (Hebrews/Israelites) as ultimately victorious, saved from annihilation, and elevated to prominence—events which would contradict an antagonistic divine stance even if God were explicitly mentioned.
